q-108946.name: Question 2
q-108946.problem:
The probability distribution of the random variable $X$ is given below. Given that $\text{E}[X]=7,$ calculate $\text{Var}[2-5X].$ 

| $x$ | $5$ | $6$ | $9$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $f(x)$ | $\frac{1}{5}$ | $\frac{2}{5}$ | $\frac{2}{5}$ |
q-108946.worked_solution:
Recall that for any random variable $X$ and constants $a$ and $b,$ we have

$$
\text{Var}[aX+b]={a}^{2}\cdot \text{Var}[X].
$$

In our case, $a=-5$ and $b=2.$ Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{Var}[2-5X] & =(-5)^{2}\cdot \text{Var}[X] \\  & =25\cdot \text{Var}[X].\end{aligned}
$$

We can compute the variance of $X$ using the following formula:

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{Var}[X]=\text{E}[{X}^{2}]-\text{E}[X]^{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Additionally, we're given that $\text{E}[X]=7.$ 

We start by computing $\text{E}[{X}^{2}].$ Summing up the products of each value of ${X}^{2}$ and its associated probability, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{E}[{X}^{2}] & ={5}^{2}\cdot f(5)+{6}^{2}\cdot f(6)+{9}^{2}\cdot f(9) \\  & =25(\frac{1}{5})+36(\frac{2}{5})+81(\frac{2}{5}) \\  & =\frac{259}{5}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{Var}[X] & =\text{E}[{X}^{2}]-\text{E}[X]^{2} \\  & =\frac{259}{5}-{7}^{2} \\  & =\frac{259}{5}-49 \\  & =\frac{14}{5}.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally,

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{Var}[2-5X] & =25\cdot \text{Var}[X] \\  & =25\cdot \frac{14}{5} \\  & =14\cdot 5 \\  & =70.\end{aligned}
$$

q-109056.name: Question 3
q-109056.problem:
The probability distribution of the random variable $X$ is given below. Given that $\text{E}[X]=2,$ calculate $\text{Var}[\sqrt{3}X].$ 

| $x$ | $0$ | $2$ | $4$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $f(x)$ | $\frac{1}{3}$ | $\frac{1}{3}$ | $\frac{1}{3}$ |
q-109056.worked_solution:
Recall that for any random variable $X$ and constant $a,$ we have

$$
\text{Var}[aX]={a}^{2}\cdot \text{Var}[X].
$$

In our case, $a=\sqrt{3}.$ Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{Var}[\sqrt{3}X] & ={\sqrt{3}}^{2}\cdot \text{Var}[X] \\  & =3\cdot \text{Var}[X].\end{aligned}
$$

We can compute the variance of $X$ using the following formula:

$$
\text{Var}[X]=\text{E}[{X}^{2}]-\text{E}[X]^{2}
$$

Additionally, we're given that $\text{E}[X]=2.$ 

We start by computing $\text{E}[{X}^{2}].$ Summing up the products of each value of ${X}^{2}$ and its associated probability, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{E}[{X}^{2}] & ={0}^{2}\cdot f(0)+{2}^{2}\cdot f(2)+{4}^{2}\cdot f(4) \\  & =4\cdot \frac{1}{3}+16\cdot \frac{1}{3} \\  & =\frac{20}{3}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{Var}[X] & =\text{E}[{X}^{2}]-\text{E}[X]^{2} \\  & =\frac{20}{3}-{2}^{2} \\  & =\frac{8}{3}.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally,

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{Var}[\sqrt{3}X] & =3\cdot \text{Var}[X] \\  & =3\cdot \frac{8}{3} \\  & =8.\end{aligned}
$$

q-109091.name: Question 5
q-109091.problem:
The probability distribution of the random variable $X$ is given below. Given that $\text{E}[X]=1,$ calculate $\text{Var}[\frac{1}{8}-\frac{1}{2}X].$ 

| $x$ | $0$ | $1$ | $3$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $f(x)$ | $\frac{1}{2}$ | $\frac{1}{4}$ | $\frac{1}{4}$ |
q-109091.worked_solution:
Recall that for any random variable $X$ and constants $a$ and $b,$ we have

$$
\text{Var}[aX+b]={a}^{2}\cdot \text{Var}[X].
$$

In our case, $a=-\frac{1}{2}$ and $b=\frac{1}{8}.$ Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{Var}[\frac{1}{8}-\frac{1}{2}X] & ={(-\frac{1}{2})}^{2}\cdot \text{Var}[X] \\  & =\frac{1}{4}\cdot \text{Var}[X].\end{aligned}
$$

We can compute the variance of $X$ using the following formula:

$$
\text{Var}[X]=\text{E}[{X}^{2}]-\text{E}[X]^{2}
$$

Additionally, we're given that $\text{E}[X]=1.$ 

We start by computing $\text{E}[{X}^{2}].$ Summing up the products of each value of ${X}^{2}$ and its associated probability, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{E}[{X}^{2}] & ={0}^{2}\cdot f(0)+{1}^{2}\cdot f(1)+{3}^{2}\cdot f(3) \\  & =1\cdot \frac{1}{4}+9\cdot \frac{1}{4} \\  & =\frac{5}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{Var}[X] & =\text{E}[{X}^{2}]-\text{E}[X]^{2} \\  & =\frac{5}{2}-{1}^{2} \\  & =\frac{3}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally,

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{Var}[\frac{1}{8}-\frac{1}{2}X] & =\frac{1}{4}\cdot \text{Var}[X] \\  & =\frac{1}{4}\cdot \frac{3}{2} \\  & =\frac{3}{8}.\end{aligned}
$$

Question 5
?

The probability distribution of the random variable X is given below. Given that E[X]=1, calculate Var[18−12X].

x 0 1 3
f(x) 12 14 14
a
38
b
−14
c
34
d
−56
e
32
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

Recall that for any random variable X and constants a and b, we have

Var[aX+b]=a2⋅Var[X].

In our case, a=−12 and b=18. Therefore,

Var[18−12X]=(−12)2⋅Var[X]=14⋅Var[X].

We can compute the variance of X using the following formula:

Var[X]=E[X2]−E[X]2

Additionally, we're given that E[X]=1.

We start by computing E[X2]. Summing up the products of each value of X2 and its associated probability, we get

E[X2]=02⋅f(0)+12⋅f(1)+32⋅f(3)=1⋅14+9⋅14=52.

Therefore,

Var[X]=E[X2]−E[X]2=52−12=32.

Finally,

Var[18−12X]=14⋅Var[X]=14⋅32=38.
